Use an AI agents and MCP application for an MCP server, or any other API, that you host and that AI agents connect to on behalf of your users. Agents sign your users in with Kinde and receive access tokens for your server's **Resource URL**.

If you want Kinde to host the MCP server and call your API for you, use an [MCP connection](/mcp-servers/) instead.

## Plan limits

The number of AI agents and MCP applications you can have depends on your Kinde plan.

| Plan       | AI agents and MCP applications               |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Free       | 1                                            |
| Pro        | 3                                            |
| Plus       | 10                                           |
| Scale      | Unlimited                                    |
| Enterprise | Unlimited, unless your contract sets a limit |

The limit applies to your whole business. Applications in every environment, such as production and staging, count toward it.

If your plan has a limit, the **AI agents and MCP** option in the application type list shows how many you have in use, for example _1 of 1 in use on your plan_.

If they're all in use when you select **Save**, Kinde offers you a plan upgrade. On a plan without an upgrade, such as Enterprise, Kinde shows an error instead. Either way, you can delete an AI agents and MCP application you no longer need, then add a new one.

If you create applications with the Kinde Management API, a request over the limit returns a `400` error with the code `PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED`.

<Aside>

The limit is checked only when you add an application. If you move to a plan with a lower limit, your existing applications keep working, but you can't add another until you're under the new limit.

</Aside>

## Trusted agent hosts

<Aside type="upgrade">

Trusted agent hosts are available on the [Kinde Plus plan or higher](https://kinde.com/pricing/).

</Aside>

Agents from Claude and ChatGPT, and agents running on a user's own machine, can connect to your application without any setup. If you build your own agent and host it on your own domain, add that domain under **Trusted agent hosts** so Kinde accepts it.

1. Go to **Settings > Environment > Applications** and select the **Customer identity** tab.
2. Select **View details** on your AI agents and MCP application.
3. In **Trusted agent hosts**, enter each domain on a new line, for example `agent.example.com`. You can add up to 10 hosts.
4. Select **Save**.

Enter a bare domain name only, without a scheme, port, path or wildcard. IP addresses and private or reserved names, such as ones ending in `.local`, `.internal` or `.test`, aren't accepted.

Only add domains you fully control. Don't add shared hosting domains, such as a pages or CDN domain, because someone else can host an agent there.

<Aside type="warning">

If you move to a plan without trusted agent hosts, the hosts you listed stay on the application but stop working. Agents on those domains are refused. So are new agent registrations with a callback URL on those domains, and callbacks on those domains for agents that already registered.

You can still remove the hosts and save the rest of the application's settings. If you upgrade again, the hosts work again once the plan change applies.

</Aside>
